learningObjectives: Install the Tricentis Mobile Agent on Windows and macOS.
Start TMA for local use versus starting it for remote use.
Locate the TMA console and use it to confirm devices are Ready before touching Tosca.
Understand which port TMA listens on and why that matters for firewalls and remote setups.

elements.term: A separate installer from Tosca Commander
elements.description: TMA is installed separately from Tosca Commander using the package for its host operating system. Local/remote deployment changes topology and configuration, not the authoring model. Windows, macOS and Linux installation steps are different; use the matching official guide.

elements.title: Install locations
items: Windows: installs under C:\Program Files\Tricentis\Mobile Agent by default.
macOS: use the matching macOS installation guide and installed Agent command; the Windows installer is not interchangeable.

elements.text: TMA 2025.4 specifies bare-metal hosts, not virtual machines. Do not infer that an unsupported VM deployment works reliably from an anecdote.

bulletPoints: TMA is its own installer, separate from Tosca Commander — install it on whichever machine will manage the devices.
TMA 2025.4: bare-metal host requirement; validate the installed version’s support matrix.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Starting TMA: tray launch vs command line

elements.description: The TMA 2025.4 CLI guide states that services bind to localhost by default. A default local start is suitable only when the caller can reach those local bindings; check actual configuration rather than assuming every customized GUI start has the same bindings.

elements.term: Command-line launch with --rest-address — required for remote use
elements.description: For the documented cross-machine connection, start with tricentis-mobile-agent start --rest-address <IP>:<port>. This binds the web server to the chosen address. Appium and gRPC have separate --appium-port and --grpc-address settings; use the endpoint required by each consumer.

elements.title: Finding and running the executable
items: Windows: the remote guide uses C:\Program Files\Tricentis\Mobile Agent and tricentis-mobile-agent.exe.
Mac/Linux: the remote guide invokes tricentis-mobile-agent start --rest-address <IP>:<port>.
Choose a reachable host binding and configured service port. Do not assume REST and Appium use the same port or that the browser UI proves session creation.

elements.text: A reachable console demonstrates access to that web endpoint, not that a device session or Appium connection will succeed. Check service bindings, network access and session logs separately.

bulletPoints: --rest-address configures the web endpoint; Appium and gRPC ports/bindings are separate.

elements.description: The Tosca configuration guide documents 8585 as the default Appium port; the TMA preparation guide also uses http://localhost:8585/ for its interface. Remote examples use a configured REST binding. Inspect the actual endpoints and permit the necessary traffic; do not infer one universal REST port from an Appium example.

elements.text: Test the required endpoint from the caller’s host and inspect Agent/session logs. A successful web response proves that specific endpoint responds; it does not prove a device is authorized or the requested session capabilities work.

bulletPoints: Appium default: 8585 in the Tosca guide. Remote REST binding: configured explicitly.
Check the necessary network paths instead of opening an assumed universal port.

elements.description: Device management lists detected devices and their information. Inspect availability before session creation, but a device entry or ready status is only one diagnostic signal. Authorization, capabilities, target app and network paths still need validation.

elements.title: First-run checklist
items: Install TMA on the machine that will manage devices.
Start it (tray for local, --rest-address for remote).
Connect a device via USB, or have an emulator/simulator already running.
Open the configured Agent interface and inspect the expected device and its availability.
Only then move to Tosca Commander to configure the connection.

bulletPoints: Inspect device availability, then validate the actual Tosca session; one status cannot isolate every root cause.

elements.description: Check the release notes and documented compatibility for the installed Agent and Tosca versions. The TMA upgrade guide installs the matching OS package to replace the previous Agent and retain configuration/devices. Version numbers do not imply a required one-to-one matching release.

bulletPoints: Use documented compatibility and release notes; do not guess a required version match.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming the tray launch enables remote access
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Starting TMA normally on a second machine, seeing its console load in a browser from the Tosca machine, and concluding remote connection is fully enabled.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For the documented cross-machine connection, start with tricentis-mobile-agent start --rest-address <IP>:<port>. This binds the web server to the chosen address. Appium and gRPC have separate --appium-port and --grpc-address settings; use the endpoint required by each consumer.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting the firewall on a Remote setup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Configuring --rest-address correctly but still getting connection failures from the Tosca machine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the configured service addresses/ports from the caller’s host and allow the required traffic. A console response alone does not verify Appium session creation or all device prerequisites.

examPitfalls.title: Jumping straight to Tosca without checking the TMA console
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Configuring the Tosca-side connection immediately after connecting a device, without confirming device status first.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Device management lists detected devices and their information. Inspect availability before session creation, but a device entry or ready status is only one diagnostic signal. Authorization, capabilities, target app and network paths still need validation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which CLI command configures the documented remote TMA web-server binding?

options.text: From the tray icon or Start Menu, same as any local install.
From the command line, using tricentis-mobile-agent start --rest-address <IP>:<port>.
TMA cannot be started manually; it must auto-detect remote Tosca instances.
Only through the TMA console's web UI, never the command line.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The remote guide uses start --rest-address <IP>:<port>. The CLI distinguishes the web endpoint from Appium and gRPC service settings; a reachable web interface does not prove session creation.

optionExplanations.A: A default local binding does not configure the documented remote address.
optionExplanations.B: This is the remote guide’s web-server binding command. Appium and gRPC settings remain separate.
optionExplanations.C: The documented CLI explicitly supports manual startup and configured bindings.
optionExplanations.D: The remote guide uses the CLI; it is not restricted to web UI startup.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What default Appium port does the Tosca mobile configuration guide document?
practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the default Appium port from a custom REST binding.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The guide documents 8585 as the default Appium port. REST binding and custom ports must be checked separately.

optionExplanations.A: 80 is not the documented default Appium port in this guide.
optionExplanations.B: 4444 is not the default specified in the Tosca mobile guide.
optionExplanations.C: 8585 is the documented default Appium port; do not generalize it to every configured REST endpoint.
optionExplanations.D: 9515 is not the documented default Appium port here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before attempting a new mobile session, which Agent-side check provides useful device-readiness evidence?

options.text: That the Tosca licence file is up to date.
That the device shows as Ready in the TMA console.
That the Mobile Scan wizard has been run at least once before.

practiceQuiz.hint: Check the expected device, then validate the session itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Inspect the expected device’s availability in Agent Device management. That is useful evidence, not proof that all network, authorization, app and capability prerequisites are healthy.

optionExplanations.A: License validity can matter, but it does not inspect Agent device availability.
optionExplanations.B: Availability in Device management is useful evidence before trying a session, without proving every prerequisite.
optionExplanations.C: Prior scanning does not establish the device’s current readiness.
optionExplanations.D: Charging alone does not establish authorized automation availability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following statements about Tricentis Mobile Agent is false?

options.text: TMA supports both direct and remote connections for devices
Every Tosca user must manually install and configure Appium and Java before using TMA.
TMA allows testing on both native and hybrid mobile apps
TMA supports connection through CLI for remote devices

practiceQuiz.hint: TMA exists specifically to remove this requirement.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TMA provides the supported bundled setup, so manual component setup is not a universal prerequisite. Platform/device preparation and version compatibility still apply.

optionExplanations.A: Direct and documented remote device connections are supported.
optionExplanations.B: This false universal requirement contradicts the Agent’s bundled setup; other device/platform preparation remains necessary.
optionExplanations.C: Native/hybrid app testing are documented supported categories.
optionExplanations.D: The CLI supports the documented remote binding workflow.

quickRecap.value: Separate OS-specific installer; follow the relevant host installation guide.
Default services bind to localhost; inspect actual configuration.
tricentis-mobile-agent start --rest-address <IP>:<port> from the command line — required for cross-machine setups.
Appium default 8585; REST binding is configured separately with --rest-address.
Inspect detected devices/availability; validate session creation separately.
TMA 2025.4 documents bare-metal hosts, not virtual machines.
Check documented Agent/Tosca compatibility and release notes; no assumed one-to-one version pairing.
